description: Packs a local folder and publishes it as a NEW app on Apprua, the user's own app server ("publish on Apprua" / "pubblica su Apprua" means this tool; the app gets its own address, https://<name>.<domain> or http://<name>.localhost). BEFORE calling: confirm with the user the app name, a one-line description, and whether the app saves data (persistent=true keeps /data across deploys). Never put secrets (API keys, passwords) in the files: use set_env after publishing. Supported: a Dockerfile, a Node/Python/... project, or a static folder with index.html. If the app needs to know who is using it (several people changing shared data, "changed by", conflicts), do not build a login: Apprua signs people in and its server side gets the headers X-Apprua-User (email), X-Apprua-User-Name (URL-encoded) and X-Apprua-Role, trusted only when the header X-Apprua-Key equals the variable APPRUA_APP_KEY; no X-Apprua-User means nobody signed in. After success, give the user the URL. On failure read the log, propose a fix, and use update_app.

description.description: What the app does, one sentence

name.description: App name = sub-domain, e.g. "my-notes" (lowercase letters, digits, dashes)

path.description: Absolute path of the local folder to publish (on this PC). If the user says "this project", use the root folder of the project you are working on

persistent.description: true if the app stores data (files/SQLite) in /data that must survive restarts and new versions

port.description: Port the app listens on, if not obvious (static sites: omit)

name: publish_app
title: Publish a new app
